title: The siege of 1565
description: Melvyn Bragg and historians on the summer of 1565, when the Ottoman fleet besieged the Knights of St. John on Malta and failed. The knights held out in Fort St. Angelo, across the Grand Harbour, and built Valletta afterward.

title: Who the Knights of Malta were
show: Everything Everywhere Daily: History, Science, Geography & More
description: How a hospital order founded in Jerusalem in the 1000s became a military order, moved to Rhodes and then Malta, and ruled the island until Napoleon took it in 1798. Its grand masters governed from this palace.

apple: Everything Everywhere Daily: History, Science, Geography & More The Knights of Malta

title: Caravaggio’s largest painting
episode: Episode 278 - Caravaggio's "The Beheading of St. John the Baptist"
description: On The Beheading of St. John the Baptist, which Caravaggio painted in 1608 for the knights’ oratory while hiding in Malta from a murder charge. It is the only painting he ever signed, in the blood on the floor.
spotify: Rebuilding The Renaissance Episode 278 - Caravaggio's "The Beheading of St. John the Baptist"

title: The island that would not be starved
episode: Malta: 'The Unsinkable Aircraft Carrier' of WWII
place: Fort St. Elmo and National War Museum
description: Historian Dan Snow on Malta in the Second World War, when its British base attacked Axis supply lines and German and Italian planes bombed it for two years. King George VI awarded the whole island the George Cross in 1942.
spotify: Dan Snow's History Hit Malta: 'The Unsinkable Aircraft Carrier' of WWII
apple: Dan Snow's History Hit Malta: 'The Unsinkable Aircraft Carrier' of WWII

title: The convoy that saved Malta
show: WW2 Pod: We Have Ways of Making You Talk
episode: The Siege Of Malta: Operation Pedestal (Part 6)
description: Historians James Holland and Al Murray on Operation Pedestal, the August 1942 convoy that fought its way to Malta. The crippled tanker Ohio was towed into the Grand Harbour on August 15, a feast day, still celebrated as the Santa Marija convoy.

title: The vote on divorce
description: In 2011 Malta, a deeply Catholic country, voted in a referendum to allow divorce, one of the last countries in the world to do so. Parliament now meets in Renzo Piano’s stone building by the city gate.
